source.title: Do Flat Minima Improve Sparse Novel View Synthesis?
source.authors: Youngsik Yun; Dongjun Gu; Youngjung Uh

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material. No relevant truncation or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: The study experimentally examines whether loss sharpness tracks generalization, using novel-view-synthesis models and sharpness measures different from the magnitude-aware measure in V7. Its results bear on that broader relationship but do not test the claim versions as specifically defined.
record.gate_note: The experiments measure sharpness and held-out novel-view error, but use 3D scene representations and novel viewpoints rather than the classification networks and magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in the versions. Record the sharpness/generalization results under fits_no_version. Other reconstruction-quality tables do not independently measure the claim's sharpness–gap relationship.
record.test_reason: The study tests a related sharpness–generalization question in sparse novel-view synthesis, but none of V1–V8. Its Hessian-eigenvalue sharpness is not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure, its subjects are scene representations rather than the specified convolutional classifiers, and it does not compare rankings against norm- or margin-based measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' interpretation: appropriate sharpness varies with local image structure, with sharpness preserved for fine details and stronger flattening used in low-detail regions. Their structure-aware optimization improves aggregate reconstruction metrics across tested frameworks and settings. These findings concern novel-view synthesis and do not establish a failure of V7's magnitude-aware measure; improvements are not universal across individual scenes.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies SAM-style sharpness regularization to 3D Gaussian Splatting and other scene-reconstruction systems; it is not a reproduction of the classification-network experiments in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The relationship between sharpness and held-out error differs across 3DGS, SAM and the proposed structure-aware method; the study also reports that the benefit varies with local image detail and view covisibility.

fits_no_version.finding: On Blender lego, SAM has lower mean Hessian sharpness than the proposed method (0.000692 versus 0.000807), but higher test error (0.03269 versus 0.03078). However, subtracting reported training errors gives SAM a slightly smaller gap (0.02115 versus 0.02151). Thus this comparison separates test-error ranking from gap ranking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In sparse novel-view synthesis, lower Hessian sharpness need not correspond to lower held-out reconstruction error.

fits_no_version.finding: On LLFF fern, SAM reduces Hessian maximum eigenvalue from 0.00281 to 0.00188 and the gap from 0.0985 to 0.0809. The proposed method has higher eigenvalue than SAM (0.00277) but a slightly smaller reported gap (0.0805). No uncertainty is supplied for these comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian sharpness does not strictly rank reconstruction generalization gaps across these sparse novel-view optimization methods.

record.problems: The experiments concern sparse novel view synthesis, not the classification or language-model settings in the versions. The sharpness measure is not magnitude-aware. The Figure 5 comparison is on the LLFF fern scene, and uncertainty is not stated for those comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Other reconstruction-quality comparisons, ablations, and supplementary results were left out because they report quality or speed without a sharpness–generalization-gap measure. Hyperparameter grid-search values were also excluded because they are selection evidence rather than outcomes bearing on the claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization and chance-level held-out random-label accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under the specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects in classifiers; Gaussian-dropping baselines do not test this version.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus classification generalization gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the reader's tests/T2 classification because its own gate note correctly identifies that no defined version is tested. Figure 1 supports a mismatch between sharpness and test-error rankings, whereas Figure 5 supplies the reported mismatch with gap rankings. The ablation prose calls direct SAM degraded, although Table 2's aggregate metrics improve over unmodified 3DGS; that wording should not be treated as numerical evidence of worse overall performance.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in image classifiers.
Width sweeps in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers on classification or language benchmarks.
Large-batch training and its generalization gap.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
The study does not use magnitude-aware sharpness, compare it with norm- and margin-based measures, or evaluate the specified convolutional-family classification setting.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
